correctness.rationale: A base-B one-parameter subgroup with B>d gives pairwise distinct weights to all degree-d monomials, so the coefficient projective fixed locus consists exactly of monomial points. A one-variable monomial defines a nonreduced hypersurface. For n>=3, every monomial using at least two variables is a union of coordinate hyperplanes with nonempty pairwise intersection and is singular there. For n=2, a monomial divisor on P^1 is reduced only when both positive exponents are one, which gives the unique smooth monomial xy at d=2. Euler localization therefore gives chi_c of the smooth locus as zero except for the single binary-quadratic fixed point, and projective additivity gives the discriminant formula. The checker independently verifies weight separation and the monomial smoothness classification over a broad finite grid.

value.rationale: The discriminant is the fundamental boundary separating smooth and singular hypersurfaces in the projective coefficient space. The theorem gives its complete ordinary Euler characteristic in every dimension and degree, identifies the unique exception, and equivalently shows that the entire coefficient-space parameter space of smooth hypersurfaces has vanishing compactly supported Euler characteristic outside one smallest case. This is a uniform structural limitation of Euler characteristic on a central moduli precursor, not a finite numerical slice.
